transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-18 16:00 PDT
Duration: 1h7m
Attendees: Alex Navarro (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood SE), Jason Lu (CTO, Arcadia), Maria Ortega (Lead ML Eng), Tom Bennett (Platform/SRE), Renee Park (PM)

Summary:
Quick scoping call to map Arcadia's conversational search workload to Redwood pilot sizing and KPIs. Focus on QPS, expected concurrency, token distributions (user prompt vs model response), tail latency targets, and benchmark plan (replay of production logs). Action items around providing logs and running a 48-hour replay benchmark.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Alex Navarro: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to get into the workload portrait so we can size the pilot and propose a benchmark plan. Jason, quick one, can you summarize the current usage pattern?
[00:12] Jason Lu: Sure uh so Arcadia's main product is the conversational insights chat on the analytics dashboard. Peak QPS right now is about 120 requests per second during business hours, um average about 30 qps, but there's a lot of burstiness, like sudden analyst sessions that drive concurrency up.
[00:28] Maria Ortega: yea and to add we're seeing many short sessions where a user sends 3-6 follow-ups, so the session-level concurrency is driving the KV cache reuse behavior which matters a lot for latency.
[00:40] Priya Shah: got it. When you say 120 peak, is that short lived bursts or sustained?
[00:44] Jason Lu: mostly short lived — 30-90s bursts when a team runs an exploratory run. Maybe 10-15% of peaks are sustained ~10 minutes.
[00:54] Jordan Li: ok that helps. Can you share average token lengths per turn? input vs output?
[00:58] Maria Ortega: average user prompt 45 tokens, median 34, but there's a heavy tail — some prompts like full SQL or pasted text go up to 3-4k tokens. Model responses average 120 tokens but with long-form answers hitting 800+ tokens occasionally.
[01:14] Alex Navarro: perfect, that token skew matters for batching and memory footprint. For sizing we usually model three cohorts: small (<64 tokens), medium (64-512), and large (>512). What percent fall in each?
[01:26] Maria Ortega: small 62%, medium 30%, large 8% — though the large are the ones that drive tail latency and GPU memory pressure.
[01:36] Tom Bennett: also note many requests include a short conversation history of ~3 turns retained which increases input side tokens by ~25-30%.
[01:44] Priya Shah: thanks Tom. For pilot success criteria, do you have a target p95 or p99 latency we should be aiming for?
[01:50] Renee Park (PM): our internal bar is p95 < 300ms and p99 < 800ms for interactive queries. For the long-form responses we're ok with higher but we want predictable tails.
[02:03] Alex Navarro: good, that's reasonable. Quick expectation setting: for a hosted inference path with batching and KV cache, reaching p95 <300ms for small/medium is achievable; p99 depends on burst concurrency and model choice. If you need p99 strong across large responses we often recommend Dedicated with pinned capacity and longer warm caches.
[02:22] Maria Ortega: can you explain the tradeoffs — dedicated vs hosted — in terms of predictability and cost?
[02:27] Alex Navarro: yeah. Hosted gives fast time-to-market and lower startup cost; we multiplex across customers so bursts are handled by routing policies. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and reserved GPUs so you get consistent p99 at the expense of a monthly commit. Also dedicated lets you pin quantized variants which can cut token cost.
[02:46] Jordan Li: another lever is prefix/KV caching — if the majority of prompts reuse recent context we can hit large effective throughput gains. But if conversations are highly unique (like pasted docs) caching is less effective.
[02:58] Maria Ortega: ours are mixed, about 40% reuse across within-session prefixes. so caching will help but not solve big large-token cases.
[03:06] Priya Shah: OK, for the benchmark plan we propose: 1) replay 48h of production logs to exercise realistic burst patterns; 2) run synthetic tails for large token cases to stress memory; 3) run concurrency sweeps to map token-latency curves at 5, 10, 25, 50, 100 concurrent sessions. Any objections?
[03:24] Jason Lu: that sounds good. Replay is key — we want to see real-world tail behavior, not just synthetic.
[03:29] Tom Bennett: network topology will matter for private deployment; we'll need to test within our VPC to account for inside-region latency and egress rules.
[03:37] Alex Navarro: noted. We'll do two benchmark lanes — hosted (Redwood-managed) and private VPC (customer-managed) to compare. For the replay we'll need 7 days of anonymized logs with sample payloads. Jason will send.
[03:48] Maria Ortega: one more nuance: our tokenization varies because users paste markdown and code; the BPE tokenization causes token counts to be noisy. We can annotate ground-truth token lengths but expect variation +/- 10%.
[04:00] Priya Shah: thanks. On compute, do you have a preference for models (open LLMs) or proprietary?
[04:05] Jason Lu: prefer open models for cost and auditability — we're looking at Mistral-like and Llama-v2 variants. Also some internal evaluation teams are experimenting with quantized variants.
[04:14] Alex Navarro: makes sense. For open models we typically benchmark H100 and A100-class instances and present throughput curves per model variant and quantization setting. We'll include INT8/4-bit runs where possible.
[04:25] Jordan Li: important to capture the token mix: we should log three fields per request in the replay: prompt_tokens, response_tokens, session_history_tokens. That lets us reconstruct memory pressure.
[04:36] Maria Ortega: yes we can add those. We'll produce a sanitized CSV mapping those fields.
[04:40] Renee Park: timeline wise, what's realistic? We need results to present to execs in early April.
[04:46] Alex Navarro: if we get logs by 3/20, Priya can run the 48h replay and initial concurrency sweeps by 3/25, then we can hand you a results deck 3/27. If you accept, we can schedule a results walkthrough first week of April.
[04:59] Jason Lu: that works. Budget question — any ballpark for cost delta between hosted and dedicated?
[05:04] Alex Navarro: rough rule: hosted cost per token is higher but with no monthly commitment; dedicated reduces unit cost but you commit to reserved GPUs. We'll send a comparative cost model; for your QPS profile with ~120 peak, a small dedicated pool might start to pay off if sustained utilization > 60%. We'll include a tipping point analysis.
[05:23] Maria Ortega: can you also include operational metrics we can surface: token-level spend, p95/p99 per model, and a breakdown by cohort (small/med/large)?
[05:31] Priya Shah: absolutely — and we'll include recommendations for batching/windowing settings, KV cache TTLs, and quantization profiles.
[05:39] Tom Bennett: security checklist — SSO/SAML, KMS for key management, audit logs retention. We need to know if Redwood supports customer-managed KMS and ability to retain logs for 1 year.
[05:49] Alex Navarro: yes we support KMS integrations and audit log export; retention windows are configurable (add-on for extended retention). We'll include the security doc and a short notes page showing SSO, RBAC, and SOC2 items.
[06:00] Renee Park: great. Any blockers for starting the replay?
[06:02] Jason Lu: nothing blocker-wise, just need to sanitize logs. We'll try to get them by end of week.
[06:07] Alex Navarro: awesome. We'll send templates for the log format and synthetic tail scenarios. Priya will share the harness link once the job is running.
[06:14] Priya Shah: one more technical note — when we replay, we simulate KV warming and cold start scenarios, plus concurrency spikes to reproduce the 30-90s bursts. We'll also capture quantile latency heatmaps and GPU utilization traces.
[06:26] Maria Ortega: perfect. Also can you capture correlation between response token length and latency quantiles — that's a key metric for our product manager.
[06:31] Priya Shah: yes, we'll include per-token-length quantiles and a conditioned p99 curve.
[06:35] Alex Navarro: wrapping up — recap of next steps and owners. Jason to send logs by 3/20. Priya will run 48h replay and post results by 3/25. Alex sends security + pricing. Tom to coordinate VPC details. Meeting adjourned.
[06:48] Jason Lu: thanks everyone.
[06:50] Renee Park: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
